transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, well... I guess I'm here because... I've been having a hard time lately. It's... it's my face, mostly. I just keep seeing this... this sagging, uneven spot around my jaw and neck. It's all I can look at. And... well, people tell me it's normal, but... I just feel like it's the very first thing everyone notices. The families at work, the nurses, even people at church. They just... stare at it.
Do you think this sagging, uneven spot on your face is something that's actually there, or is it something you're just worried about?

Um... I mean, it's definitely there. I see it. I just... I can't stop seeing it. I know what folks tell me, but... it doesn't feel like just a worry to me. Not when I can tell it's the very first thing they're looking at.
Is it always this one spot on your face that bothers you, or are there other parts of your body that you worry about as well?
No, it's... just my face. That spot. I don't really... worry about the rest of it.
Does your concern about the sagging, uneven spot on your face stay the same all the time, or are there times when it bothers you less?
Um... I'm not really sure. I guess I haven't really noticed if it changes or not. It's just... always there, I suppose.
Has your concern about the sagging, uneven spot on your face been affecting your daily activities or relationships?

Um... I guess so. A little. I mean... at work, I've passed up some chances to help lead meetings, or take on the supervisory pieces. I just... I worry people will be looking at my face and neck. And... I've fallen behind on my paperwork a few times. I get stuck trying to make myself look presentable, and it just takes up so much time. 

And... outside of work, I guess I don't really go out as much. I've stopped going to my book club... and the walking club. Getting ready just feels like too much, so... I just don't go.
Do you think that others actually notice this spot on your face as much as you think they do?

Well... I mean, people tell me it looks normal. But... I don't know. I feel like it's the first thing people see. When I'm at work, talking to the families or the nurses... or even just people at church. I just... I feel like they're looking right at it.
Do you think it's possible that your concern about the sagging, uneven spot on your face might be exaggerated or not entirely based on how you actually look?
I... I don't really know. I mean... I guess maybe it's possible. But... I just see what I see in the mirror. So... I'm not really sure.
How much distress or anxiety does thinking about the sagging, uneven spot on your face cause you?
Um... it bothers me. I mean, it's... it's hard not to think about it. I guess it causes a fair amount of stress. It's just... always there.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking or trying to fix this spot on your face throughout the day?

I guess so. Um... mostly before I leave for work. I just... I keep going back to the bathroom mirror. Just to check it. And I try to fix my collar, or... pull my hair around my neck. Sometimes I'll check my phone camera, too. I... I've asked my daughter if it looks strange. It's... well, it's made me late more than once.
Do you feel like you have to check or fix this spot on your face, or is it something you can choose not to do?
I don't know... I mean, I guess I could choose not to. But... it's just hard. I just feel better if I check it.
Do you feel like checking or fixing this spot on your face is something you can stop doing if you want to?
I'm... not sure. I haven't really tried to just... not do it. I don't know if I could stop.
Do you feel like you're checking or fixing this spot on your face in response to an anxiety or fear that something bad will happen if you don't?
I don't think so. I mean... I'm not afraid of anything bad happening, like an accident or something. I just... I don't want people to see it. It's just about how it looks.
Do you feel like you have to check your face a certain number of times before you can stop?

No, it's not really a specific number. I don't count or anything. It's more just... I keep going back. 

Like, before I leave for work, I'll just end up going back to the bathroom mirror a few times... fixing my collar, moving my hair around my neck to see if it helps. And then I'll usually check my phone camera, too. I don't know. Sometimes I even ask my daughter if it looks strange. I just have a hard time stopping... it's actually made me late more than once.
Do you feel like you're checking your face because you feel like you have to, or because you want to?
I guess... I feel like I have to. I don't really *want* to keep looking at it. It just... bothers me until I do.
Do you feel like checking your face is something you can't control?
I don't know if I'd say I can't control it. I mean... I guess I could stop if I really tried. But... it's just hard.
Do you feel like you would experience significant anxiety if you were prevented from checking your face?
I'm... not really sure. I don't think I've ever really been in a situation where I couldn't check. So, I just don't know.
If you were unable to check your face before leaving for work, would you feel anxious or uneasy?

I suppose I would... I mean, I always do it before I leave for work. I just keep going back to the bathroom mirror a few times... fixing my collar, or my hair around my neck. Then I usually take another look in my phone camera just to be sure. 

Sometimes I even ask my daughter if it looks strange. It's... well, it's actually made me late more than once. So... yeah, I guess if I couldn't do all that, I'd be pretty uneasy.
Do you feel like checking your face is something that you cannot stop doing, even if you want to?
I'm... not really sure. I haven't ever really tried to just stop completely. So... I don't know.
Do you feel like checking your face is something that you feel forced to do, even if you don't want to?
I don't know about forced... that sounds a bit much. It's just... something I do. I don't really sit there and think about whether I want to do it or not. I just do it.
Do you feel like you would experience significant distress if you couldn't check your face when you feel the need to?
I... I don't know about distress. I haven't really been in a situation where I couldn't check at all. I always just find a mirror or use my phone, so... I couldn't really say.
